WELCOME TO THE GARAGE

Build. Race. Learn. Repeat.

  1. Build within $8,000. Open any Modify panel to learn the physics, compare packages and explore graphs before installing.
  2. Pick a shift RPM. The driver shifts automatically at your chosen threshold. Watch the power and torque curves.
  3. Predict, launch and steer. Use left/right arrows or the steering buttons to dodge barriers. Your build time is saved at 600 m. Keep driving after the checkpoint: obstacles get closer together until you crash. Survival distance is separate from the build score. Retry as often as you like.
  4. Revise with evidence. Try changing one variable at a time. Use each run to test your prediction and improve your build.

Your garage and attempts are saved in this browser. “New session” clears the notebook for a fresh start. Export your results before sharing a device.

UNDER THE HOOD

A model you can reason with.

Engine torque, gear ratios, tire grip, rear-wheel weight transfer, mass, air drag and rolling resistance determine acceleration. Gear changes interrupt driving force.

This classroom model uses illustrative engine curves and rounded parts prices. It assumes an ideal launch clutch and traction control; grip-limited time is not wheelspin. Player steering and collisions are arcade mechanics. The build is scored at 600 m; afterward the same forward physics continues while obstacle spacing shrinks. Survival distance is separate from build time; lateral tire forces are not modeled. Engine audio is synthesized from RPM, with two firing pulses per revolution, not a recording. It omits turbo lag, tire heating, wind and rotational inertia.

More grip and more power can complement each other. Lightweight and aerodynamic parts can be poor value on a short course. Not every expensive upgrade earns its price.

For teachers: completed attempts are stored locally, not enforced by a server. “New session” is an intentional reset for shared devices. This is a standalone, unofficial educational activity with no connection to Rockstar Games.
